title: Transparent entitlement rollback and pro-rata refund policy
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: PRD: Define a clear, auditable policy and implementation plan for rolling back entitlements (quota increases, feature grants, reserved credits) and issuing pro‑rata refunds or credits when customers downgrade, when we reverse a mistaken grant, or when an incident causes over-provisioning. This ticket scopes the product rules, API surface, UI changes on Console, billing ledger implications, and acceptance criteria for engineering and billing teams.
objective: Provide predictable, explainable financial outcomes for entitlement reversals so customers and CS teams can trust invoice accuracy while minimizing manual interventions and edge-case disputes.
scope: Define policy rules for three primary rollback scenarios: customer-initiated downgrade mid-cycle, admin/platform-initiated rollback (e.g., fraud/misconfiguration), and incident-driven full/partial credits.
Specify pro‑rata calculation method for time-based entitlements and compute/credit-based entitlements (tokens, embedding units, compute credits).
Design API endpoints and Console workflows for viewing pending rollbacks, approving automatic refunds, and issuing credits to accounts.
Billing ledger schema changes required to record original invoice, reversal line items, and resulting credit balances.
Acceptance tests and simulation harness to validate invoice/credit math across edge cases (multi-plan, overlapping entitlements, timezone boundaries).
out_of_scope: Pricing model redesign — we assume existing plan prices and SKU definitions remain unchanged.
Legacy invoice re‑opens beyond a 180-day dispute window (policy will reference finance SLA).
Automated chargebacks to external payment processors (finance team handles settlement flows).
requirements: R1: Rollback types must be classified and tagged in the ledger (customer_downgrade, admin_reversal, incident_credit).
R2: Pro‑rata refunds for time-bound plans use a daily-granularity approach by default; hourly granularity optional for Reserved Capacity purchases.
R3: Credits applied to account must show both the gross reversal and net effect on outstanding balance with links to original invoice lines.
R4: Console must surface a preview of the refund/credit calculation before commit and allow a single-step confirm/undo for admins within 24 hours.
R5: API must provide endpoints to simulate and then execute a rollback; simulation mode returns breakdown and ledger line IDs.
R6: All rollbacks must produce an immutable audit trail entry and reference the actor (user id or system incident id).
R7: Automated rollbacks triggered by incidents must queue for review if the credit amount exceeds a threshold configurable per-customer (default $1,000).
billing_acceptance_criteria: BAC-1: Given a mid-cycle downgrade from Plan A to Plan B, the system produces a simulated pro‑rata credit and a final credit invoice line; the credited dollar amount equals expected manual spreadsheet calculation within a tolerance of $0.01.

BAC-2: When an admin reverses a previously granted 100k compute-credit bundle due to misconfiguration, ledger shows original grant line, reversal line, and resulting balance; customer-facing invoice shows applied credit.
BAC-3: Incident-triggered credits are tagged with incident ID; for credits > threshold, the rollback remains in 'Pending Approval' state and not applied until approved via Console.

BAC-4: Console preview screen shows line-level mapping between original invoice, reversal lines, and post-credit balance with a one-click 'Apply credit' button and a visible 24-hour undo window for admins.
BAC-5: API simulation endpoint returns numeric breakdown and a unique simulation_id; executing with that simulation_id creates immutable ledger entries that match the simulation output.

BAC-6: End-to-end test suite validates 10 canonical scenarios (upgrade/downgrade same-day, mid-cycle upgrade then downgrade, overlapping reserved capacity, cross-plan entitlements, currency rounding edge cases) with deterministic invoice outcomes.
BAC-7: Finance reconciliation doc shows no net revenue mismatch beyond rounding tolerance when comparing pre-rollback and post-rollback ledgers for 100 sampled accounts.
BAC-8: Customer notification triggers (email + in-Console banner) are generated for any applied credit exceeding $50 and include an explanation and link to a help article.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Product and Finance review sign-off on policy wording and edge-case table.
AC-2: Legal confirms refund window and consumer protection compliance for target markets (NA + EU).
AC-3: Engineering provides API and ledger migrations in a staging environment with migration rollback plan.
AC-4: QA validates the simulation and execution endpoints against the test harness and signs off on stability for the targeted release.
AC-5: CS playbook and canned messaging prepared for common scenarios and reviewed by Support leadership.
AC-6: Observability: add dashboards that surface pending rollbacks, applied credits per day, and rollback approval queue length.
AC-7: Rollout: feature flag gated, initial rollout to 10% of accounts (internal + pilot customers) before global enablement.
dependencies: PM-31415 (metering snapshot windows) - need aligned definitions of billing windows
ENG-24102 (ledger v2) - ledger schema and immutability guarantees
ENG-25210 (console payments UI) - preview/apply/undo UI components
FIN-ops (finance automation) - settled process for refund settlement and PCI interactions
design_considerations: Prefer simulation-first UX to reduce disputes; explicit confirmation required for financial actions.
Keep UI language non-technical for customers while exposing full line-item detail for CS/Finance roles.
Use consistent rounding rules across currencies (round half away from zero) and record pre- and post-rounding amounts in ledger lines.
Allow per-customer override thresholds and manual reconciliation hooks for enterprise accounts via Support console.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Spec freeze and compliance sign-offs (2 weeks).
Phase 1: Engineering build + ledger migration in staging (3 weeks).
Phase 2: QA and finance reconciliation tests (1 week).
Phase 3: Pilot rollout to internal accounts and three pilot customers (2 weeks).
Phase 4: Gradual 10% -> 50% -> 100% rollout with monitoring and quick rollback flag (4 weeks).
notes: Design note: include a 'why was this credit issued' freeform field on credit entries so CS can inject customer-facing context.
Operational note: create a billing-runbook for emergency manual refunds that can't be automated.
Edge case: overlapping rollbacks (two rollbacks touching same invoice lines) must serialize and produce a single reconciled outcome; define deterministic ordering (time-of-action).
